Getting Started

In the first 20 minutes: create the folder structure, fill SECURITY.md, populate the core files in order, and run your first session in the right mode sequence.

Step 1 — Copy the starter kit

ADDF provides a standard folder structure that makes the operating model visible.

  • The core project brain files at the root
  • A docs/ folder for architecture documentation
  • A research/ folder for Research Mode output
  • A planning/ folder containing backlog and sprint subfolders
  • A src/ folder where Develop Mode writes code
Rule: The folder structure should make the operating model visible.

Step 2 — Fill SECURITY.md first

SECURITY.md defines what is and is not safe to load into an AI session. Fill the "never load" list for your project before populating any other file (e.g. .env, credentials).

Rule: Fill SECURITY.md before loading files into an AI session.

Step 3 — Populate the core files in order

The core files form a dependency chain. Fill them in this sequence:

  1. SECURITY.md
  2. AGENTS.md
  3. DOMAIN.md
  4. STATE.md
  5. COMMANDS.md
  6. DECISIONS.md
  7. QUESTIONS.md
  8. RISKS.md
Rule: If a model needs to know it later, write it to the project brain.

Step 4 — Your first session

A new project starts with this mode sequence: Research Mode → Design Mode (project memory) → Design Mode (sprint pack) → Develop Mode (dry run) → Develop Mode (implementation) → Design Mode (review & state).

Rule: Declare the mode before the model acts.
